 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Judgment:

This appeal is preferred by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 01.06.2012 passed in O.P.No.517 of 2009 by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge at Nalgonda (for short 'the Tribunal), whereby the Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.5,68,200/- towards compensation as against the claim of Rs.10,00,000/-.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge at Nalgonda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The Tribunal, vide order dated 01.06.2012 in O.P.No.517 of 2009, has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.4,600/- per month, who was working as driver and leased out his jeep and accordingly, calculated the compensation.
3. As can be seen from the said order, the accident occurred in the year 2009 and at that relevant point of time, the income of the deceased as a driver can be taken as Rs.5,500/- per month.

Accordingly, this Court deems it appropriate to consider the income of the deceased at Rs.5,500/-
per month.
4. Insofar as the deduction towards personal and living expenses is concerned, the deceased was married and survived by wife, two children and mother, therefore, total dependents are four.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 1 , the standard deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one- fourth.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. In National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others 2, the Hon'ble Apex Court at paragraph 59.4 held that in case the deceased was self-employed, additionally 25% of the income should be awarded towards future prospects, where the deceased age was below 50 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 48 years, 25% of monthly income of the deceased can be taken towards future prospects.

6. With regard to the multiplier, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (1 supra), the appropriate multiplier in the present case is '13' for the age groups of 46 to 50.
1 (2009) 6 SCC 121 2 (2017) 16 SCC 680 7.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anjali and others v. Lokendra Rathod and others 3, decided on 06.12.2022, taking into consideration the decision of Sarala Verma (supra) and also the case of Rapolu Chandrakala And 3 Ors vs D.Eranna And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22614183/

has awarded a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards loss of consortium.

8. In view of the above discussion, the compensation amount is enhanced as under:

Total compensation Rs.10,10,375/-

3 2023(1) ALD 107(SC)
9.

At this stage, learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the claimants claimed only a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- as compensation and the quantum of compensation which is now awarded would go beyond the claim made which is impermissible under law.

In view of the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Laxman @ Laxman Mourya v. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited and another 4 and in Nagappa v. Gurudayal Singh 5 , the claimants are entitled to get more amount than what has been claimed.

entities.text: Laxman @ Laxman Mourya v. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the Motor Vehicles Act being a beneficial piece of legislation, where the interest of the claimants is a paramount consideration, the Courts should always endeavour to extend the benefit to the claimants to a just and reasonable extent.
10. In the result, the appeal is allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.5,68,200/- to Rs.10,10,375/-.

The enhanced amount shall be deposited by the respondents jointly and severally within a period of two (2) months from the date of receipt of a Rapolu Chandrakala And 3 Ors vs D.Eranna And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22614183/
2 copy of this judgment.

sentences.text: The enhanced compensation amount shall 4 (2011) 10 SCC 756 5 2003 ACJ 12 (SC) carry interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
The claimants are entitled to the apportionment of the amount as directed by the Tribunal.
On such deposit, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the amount without furnishing any security.
However, the claimants are directed to deposit the deficit Court fee on the enhanced amount.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, pending if any, shall stand closed.
